notes: Units were aligned by anchor/sentence overlap; three adjacent-sentence pairs per ICS course (staff-communication rationale, 'solely by you', 'do your own work' rationale) were matched by hand, since both coders coded the same rule from neighbouring sentences. Stance agreed on all 5 documents. MAIN PATTERN 1, actor on general statements (most of the actor disagreements): in the DTEI example statements, Coder A coded facts about LLM bias/hallucination/limits as actor=student and Coder B as actor=all. Resolved to student, because these sentences sit inside syllabus templates addressed to students ('you'); the codebook defines actor as who the policy is addressed to. Same rule for the Example 4 meeting requirement ('you will need to meet with me' -> student). The DTEI syllabus page's general statements about AI's varying pedagogical role were resolved to all/general, since they are not addressed to one group. ICS 'humanity at its center' -> all. PATTERN 2, split vs merged units: in Example 3 Coder A merged the five citation/discussion questions into two units; Coder B coded one unit per question. Kept B's split (CODEBOOK: one policy per unit), so B's 'What was your prompt?', 'follow-up questions', 'What did you learn?' units were kept as only-B. Senate 'Differentiating among these cases will guide student efforts' kept as its own rationale unit. Only-B lead-in 'If you choose to use ZotGPT ... you MUST do the following' kept (it states the conditional requirement). Dropped B 'AI is a tool, just like a pencil or a computer' as framing for the adjacent disclosure rule, not a rule itself. PATTERN 3, modality on discretion and expectation wording: 'content of the policy is at the discretion of the instructor' resolved to may (it grants the instructor latitude). DTEI 'all instructors are expected to' develop/communicate/ensure resolved to should (B), following the literal 'expected to' on a teaching-center page; the binding Senate/Graduate Council requirement is coded must in its own units. Resource pointers (Senate examples link, Mollick primer) resolved to informs. 'This conversation will include knowledge checks' resolved to must, like the other 'I will' procedural commitments in the same templates. 'Cite everything, otherwise you are likely violating' phase -> during-work (the instruction is to cite). PATTERN 4, policy_type: considering whether AI facilitates or impedes learning per task -> P04 (it is advice on setting assignment-level rules, not a P41 rationale). 'Explain what aspects of learning the policy safeguards' -> P09 (syllabus content advice). 'Describe how the policy will be enforced' -> P37 (state consequences in advance) over P36. ZotGPT as 'student proxy' -> P41/general (a rationale for the ban, not itself a P19 rule). 'Explain how/what you used at the end of assignments' -> P26, matching the agreed coding of the parallel Example 4 end-of-work paragraph. NEW TYPE: Coder B proposed NEW:Human-written course communication for ICS 33/H32 'those words should be yours (and yours alone)'; Coder A had P18. Kept it as a distinct NEW type. P18 splits AI permissions for prose versus code. This rule makes no such split (the courses ban all AI anyway). It governs the communication channel between students and staff (emails and messages sent for a human reply), which is not submitted work, so P19 does not fit either. Also applied to the only-B unit 'let's have it be a two-way human conversation' (actor all). The instructor side of the same pledge stays P47, as both coders coded it; a later codebook revision could fold both sides into one 'human-to-human course communication' type. Normalized text: where either coder left policy null and the anchor fully states the rule, null was kept; in the tier document Coder B's '(Example N)' prefixes were kept so tier-specific rules stay attributable.
